messages:
jen (support): FYI Helios escalated — they saw a big p99 jump and throughput drop in us-west-2 starting ~10:12 PDT. Stack: gpt-small-qa, pinned v2.3. Customer impact: interactive widgets time out. Can someone triage? :exclamation:

alice (eng-runtime): On it. Do we have a trace ID or a link to their request logs? Any config changes around that time?

jen (support): Trace IDs: trace:hel-47f12, trace:hel-47f13. No config changes on their side. They said they didn't change model or request shape. Posting a snippet from their logs:
```
[10:12:05] req=hel-47f12 model=gpt-small-qa seq_len=512 tokens=200 latency=812ms backend=pool-3 instance=i-0b3 err=none
[10:12:07] req=hel-47f13 model=gpt-small-qa seq_len=128 tokens=60 latency=740ms backend=pool-3 instance=i-0b3
```

ben (perf): Thanks. Can someone run a quick micro-benchmark against that model on a staging box with similar seq distribution? I want p50/p90/p99 and CPU/GPU counters. Suggested command:
```
run_bench --model gpt-small-qa --seq-dist "512:0.25,128:0.75" --qps 40 --duration 300 --collect-counters
```

carlos (sre): I checked infra metrics. KVCACHE hit rate for pool-3 dropped from 86% -> 21% at ~10:11. Also saw an increase in nvlink retries on i-0b3. I'm investigating any kernel selector flaps.

alice (eng-runtime): nvlink retries could account for stalls. Also, kernel-selector recently had a small change to prefer fp16-int8 path for the attention kernel — maybe falling back causing reinitialization. Can someone grep deploy logs around 10:10 for kernel selection decisions?

deploy-bot: Deployed config/kernel-selector v1.8.2 to pool-3 at 07:02 PDT — no recent deploys at 10:10.

ben (perf): I ran the bench on a repro instance (staging-usw2-4). Results (short): p50=78ms, p90=162ms, p99=710ms — reproduces the p99 tail. Counters show long stalls on attention kernel when seq=512. Attaching the micro-flame summary:
```
attention_kernel: 72% stall_time
kv_cache_ops: 9% idle
memcopy: 6%
```

dana (product): Helios reports spikes mainly on longer queries (>=400 tokens). They're seeing frontend retries. What's the customer-facing mitigation? Can we suggest batching tweaks or fallback to a smaller context?

alice (eng-runtime): Short term: enable per-customer kv_cache warmup and reduce max_seq for the route to 384 as a mitigant. I'll open a canary rollback for kernel-selector preference if SRE confirms it correlates.

carlos (sre): Confirmed correlation: kernel-selector logs show intermittent selection failures and fallback sequences starting 10:09 on i-0b3. I'll cordon that instance and trigger a graceful drain. Also raising an incident if Helios impact is severe.

jen (support): Customer accepted a temporary config change to cap seq at 384 for their traffic. They'll monitor.

alice (eng-runtime): Action items:
- ben: run a focused perf run with nvlink stress toggled (assigned)
- carlos: cordon + drain i-0b3 and keep an eye on nvlink errors
- dana: coordinate customer comms & confirm mitigation applied
- me: prepare a canary rollback for kernel-selector pref change

ben (perf): Doing bench now with nvlink stress on/off, posting results in ~20m.

carlos (sre): i-0b3 cordoned at 10:46, draining connections. NVLink error counter reset and starting to trend back to baseline.

dana (product): Helios confirmed improved tail after seq cap; p99 down to ~230ms but still above target. They accepted a scheduled maintenance window if we need to reboot the node.

alice (eng-runtime): Thanks all. Please add any logs/traces to the incident so we can do a postmortem. I'll follow up with a root cause writeup after perf results. :eyes:

jen (support): Noted — will keep the thread updated with customer feedback.

ben (perf): Quick results: with nvlink stress enabled p99 ~900ms, without stress p99 ~220ms. Looks like hardware flakiness on nvlink path amplified by large-context attention kernel. Recommend replacing i-0b3 and promoting a clean instance.

carlos (sre): Replacement in progress, initial tests good. Moving to resolved when Helios confirms stable 24h.

jen (support): Helios reports normal behavior after the node replacement and seq cap removal. Closing the loop. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
